newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-London shares inch to election high.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-London shares inch to election high.

text.p: Share prices in London inched to a new closing high on Thursday after being moribund for most of the session with most traders unwilling to commit themselves until the outcome of Britain's general election emerges on Friday.

Trading was minimal elsewhere, too, with most of Europe's key financial markets other than London closed for the May 1 holiday, though the dollar made a foray to fresh multi-year high against the yen only to go into a sharp retreat.
London's FTSE index of blue chip shares ended up nine points at a new closing peak of 4,445.0, just 0.7 points above the previous closing high of 4,444.3 on March 11.
But traders were wondering what will happen on Friday if the latest opinion polls are right and the opposition Labour party ends 18 years of Conservative rule.
"Thoughts are turned now to the size of the (Labour) majority," one said.
Some said the FTSE could fall sharply if Labour, which has held a long and commanding lead in opinion polls, has a "landslide" victory.
"People keep saying the market has discounted a Labour government. But if the Tories (ruling Conservative Party) are wiped out, there will be a knee-jerk reaction," one trader said.

London shares drew early comfort from Wall Street's third day of gains which carried the Dow Jones Industrial Average above 7,000 for the first time in seven weeks on Wednesday, when it rose 46.96 points to close at 7,008.99.
But Wall Street remained capricious and was down around 50 points when London closed on Thursday.

Traders on both sides of the Atlantic continued scrutinise U.S. indicators, the latest of which showed that American consumers steadily boosted their spending during March, though the week's big figure comes on Friday with U.S. jobs data for April.

The U.S. Federal Reserve central bank plays close attention to jobs figures in gauging inflation pressures. It has nudged rates higher once already this year to counter inflation and meets again to review policy on May 20.
Figures on Thursday for the last week of April showed that U.S. unemployment rose faster than expected, however.
In currencies, the dollar suffered a bout of position-adjustment selling at the European close, dropping sharply against both the mark and the yen.

Dealers said the release of the U.S. of the National Association of Purchasing Managers' report for April, showing a drop in activity and in the prices index served as an excuse to sell dollars as the data cast further doubt about a U.S. interest rate rise in the near-term.
"The selling was due to market positioning," said Peter von Maydell, senior currency economist at UBS. The dollar adjusted to the Treasury market's movements this week, he said.
Stop-loss selling on both dollar/mark and dollar/yen pushed the U.S. currency below 1.72 marks and close to 126 yen.

Vague talk about central bank intervention on dollar/yen circulated in the forex market but dealers said the dollar came under pressure from selling by big funds, mainly out of the U.S., and options-related selling.
In late trade, the dollar was at 1.7182 marks, down over a pfennig from its session highs at 1.7334. Against the yen it was at 126.57 yen, down from a fresh 55-month peak at 127.47.

The British pound, meanwhile, was steady against the dollar as the market awaited the results of the parliamentary elections. It was trading at about 1.6241 dollars compared with 1.6225 late on Wednesday.

The Irish pound remained under pressure after its slide on Wednesday amid speculation that the Irish authorities are now keen to allow the currency to weaken toward its central rate in the European exchange rate mechanism at 2.4111 marks in preparation for European monetary union in 1999. It was at 2.5632 compared with 2.5950 late in European trading on Wednesday. STOCKS CLOSING PRICES
London's FTSE 100 closed up nine points at 4,445.0
The Paris CAC-40 index was closed for the May 1 holiday after finishing up 36.60 points on Wednesday at 2,639.46.
Frankfurt's DAX index was also closed after finishing up 54.88 points at 3,474.98 on Wednesday.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7182 marks compared with 1.7312 marks in late European trade on Wednesday. It was at 126.57 yen compared with 126.93 late on Wednesday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $340.80 compared with Wednesday's close of $339.65 an ounce in London.
